name: lcdf-typetools
why: Lets you open up and manipulate OpenType and multiple-master font internals, a door into font file structure.

brief.what_it_is: LCDF Typetools is a set of eleven command-line programs for reading and rewriting the internals of PostScript Type 1, Type 1 Multiple Master, OpenType (CFF and TrueType flavored) and TrueType fonts. Inputs are font files (PFA/PFB, OTF/TTF, AMFM and AFM for multiple masters). Outputs vary by tool: Type 1 fonts converted from CFF (cfftot1), AFM metrics files (mmafm, t1rawafm), single-master instances of multiple-master fonts (mmpfb), TeX TFM metrics and encodings (otftotfm), Type 42 wrappers (ttftotype42), PostScript test pages (t1testpage), and plain-text feature or codepoint reports (otfinfo). Some tools also check (t1lint) or modify (t1reencode, t1dotlessj) existing Type 1 fonts.
brief.why_it_exists: The author, Eddie Kohler, built it to make Adobe OpenType and multiple-master fonts usable from TeX and other UNIX font toolchains. The homepage says the package was made to let multiple master fonts 'work with UNIX programs for single-master fonts, like afm2tfm, ps2pk, GhostScript ps2pdf, and the X11 Type 1 font server.'
brief.how_it_works: Each program is a separate C command-line tool that parses one font format and emits another or a report. Otftotfm interprets OpenType glyph positioning, substitution and ligature tables as far as it can and writes TeX metrics and encoding files, optionally activating features you name. Mmafm and mmpfb generate a specific instance of a multiple master font from its weight and width parameters.

brief.install_notes: Source build: run ./configure then make, or ./bootstrap.sh first if you cloned from GitHub. Otftotfm can use the Kpathsea library for TeX directory integration; if Kpathsea sits in a nonstandard place, pass --with-kpathsea=PREFIX. Individual programs can be left out with --disable-PROGNAME. Mmafm needs AFM files for each master either alongside the AMFM file (named FONTNAME.afm) or listed in a PSres.upr file located through the PSRESOURCEPATH environment variable. The homepage also points to prebuilt packages from others: Homebrew, MacPorts, Fink, Debian packages, Linux RPMs, and a Windows build inside W32TeX.
brief.standout: Lets you open a commercial OpenType or multiple master font and get its features, glyph encodings and metrics out as ordinary TeX or PostScript files. Otftotfm's use of the font's own substitution and positioning tables, instead of a hand-written mapping, is what separates it from simpler converters.
brief.status: Probably maintained, but the date is unverified. The homepage lists version 2.110 as the latest release, with a changelog entry for it, and the GitHub README says the copyright runs to 2023. I did not see a release date or last-commit date.
brief.caveats: The author says he does not support Windows ports. The GitHub README describes the software as GPL version 2 only. The homepage describes t1testpage as 'preliminary software'. Installation needs a C toolchain and a configure/make build; Homebrew is the only package manager named as an install route on Mac. The mmafm and mmpfb tools need specific companion files (AMFM and AFM, or PFA/PFB multiple master fonts) that are not included with the package. The brew caveats field is empty.
